newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Nano urges president to quit.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Nano urges president to quit.

text.p: Albanian opposition politician Fatos Nano on Monday joined calls for President Sali Berisha to quit following weeks of armed unrest in the Balkan country.
Berisha on Sunday announced a pardon for Nano, the leader of the opposition Socialist Party who was freed from prison last week.
Nano, jailed in 1993 on corruption charges which the opposition said were politically inspired, was among 51 prisoners with less than two years to serve who were pardoned by presidential decree.
Nano, who was briefly prime minister in 1991, has been mentioned as a possible successor to Berisha, who is under increasing pressure at home and abroad to step down.

In an interview with the British Broadcasting Corporation, Nano threw his support behind the newly formed national unity government of Prime Minister Bashkim Fino as the best way of returning Albania to normality.
Asked about Berisha, Nano said: "I would prefer personally to shake hands with him as an Albanian but not as a president."
Nano added: "He should answer the demands of the people to step aside."
Asked if he had been involved in corruption, as the charges against him had stated, Nano answered: "No."
Rebels who control the south of the country are demanding Berisha's resignation, blaming him for allowing dubious savings schemes that failed, bankrupting thousands of families.
The Albanian government is beginning to restore order after weeks of gun law that erupted after angry citizens looted military arsenals.
Sources in the new all-party government headed by Bashkim Fino, a Socialist, said Nano had been in hiding since his release from jail and had been waiting for a pardon before reemerging in public.

He was released along with all other prisoners apart from those serving life sentences after the justice minister ruled that their security could no longer be guaranteed because of the anarchy sweeping the country.

Nano said that other prisoners in the Tirana jail from which he was released had held him a virtual hostage for 20 hours before he was let go because they realised that they would only be freed if he was.
Eventually the prison governor provided him with a car and an official escort to take him home.
